project.title: Cross-Department Protocol for High-Risk Detainee Health Monitoring
project.objective: Design and roll out a standard protocol to monitor, document, and communicate health risks for detainees, improving safety, compliance, and operational coordination.
deliverables: End-to-end detainee health monitoring process map
Standard operating procedure (SOP) for health risk assessment and escalation
Screening and observation checklists for officers and staff
Centralised health monitoring log template and filing workflow
Training and briefing materials for custody staff and assistants
Pilot evaluation report with improvement recommendations
constraints: Must comply with correctional procedures and legal use-of-force rules
No changes to core IT systems; use existing tools and paper forms
Protocol must be usable across shifts with minimal extra workload
All documentation must respect privacy and data protection rules
Pilot must be completed within one full rota cycle
Training time per staff member limited to 2 hours

risks.risk: Staff perceive the new protocol as extra bureaucracy and do not adopt it consistently.
risks.mitigation: Co-design forms with officers, keep them short, and include quick wins in training to show value.

risks.risk: Health and security information is not shared correctly between officers and admin staff.
risks.mitigation: Define clear handover points, shared terminology, and a simple logging template reviewed in training.

risks.risk: Protocol conflicts with existing correctional procedures or legal constraints.
risks.mitigation: Early review with compliance and legal, adjust SOP wording, and document alignment with current rules.

risks.risk: Paper-based logs are incomplete or lost, reducing auditability.
risks.mitigation: Introduce a central filing routine, daily spot checks by a supervisor, and a simple index sheet.

risks.risk: Health risk indicators are not well understood by non-medical staff.
risks.mitigation: Biophysicist prepares a plain-language guide and examples; include scenario-based exercises in training.

themes.theme: Operational feasibility on the prison floor
themes.why_relevant: Protocol must work during real patrols, inspections, and incidents without slowing response.
Logs and SOPs must stand up to audits and legal review while staying practical.

themes.theme: Health risk indicators and early warning signs
themes.why_relevant: Biophysicist expertise is needed to define simple, reliable observation criteria.
Officers, assistants, and medical staff must share consistent information across shifts.
Staff need concise training and clear messages to adopt the new protocol quickly.

backlog.task: Map current detainee health monitoring and incident escalation process
definition_of_done: Process map drafted covering intake, routine checks, and incidents
Validated with at least one prison officer and one manager
Gaps and pain points listed in a short note

backlog.task: Define simple health risk indicators and observation criteria for officers
definition_of_done: List of key physical and behavioural indicators created
Indicators translated into plain language suitable for non-medical staff
Reviewed and accepted by prison officer representative

backlog.task: Draft standard operating procedure (SOP) for health risk assessment and escalation
definition_of_done: SOP document includes roles, steps, and escalation paths
Checked for alignment with correctional procedures
Feedback from prison officer and compliance captured and integrated

backlog.task: Design screening and observation checklists for intake and routine patrols
definition_of_done: Checklist layout designed for quick use on paper
Includes health indicators and security observations
Pilot version printed and tested with at least two officers

backlog.task: Create centralised health monitoring log template and filing workflow
definition_of_done: Log template created for daily use
Filing and indexing routine defined and documented
Trial run completed for three days with sample data

backlog.task: Develop training and briefing materials for custody staff
definition_of_done: Slide deck or handout explaining protocol and indicators prepared
Includes 2–3 short scenarios for discussion
Reviewed by a management assistant for clarity and length

backlog.task: Plan and schedule pilot implementation in one unit
definition_of_done: Pilot scope, dates, and participating staff agreed with prison management
Briefing sessions scheduled and invites sent
Success criteria for pilot documented

backlog.task: Run pilot and collect feedback from officers and assistants
definition_of_done: Pilot executed for agreed period
Feedback gathered from at least three officers and two assistants
Key issues and suggestions summarised in a short report

backlog.task: Refine forms and visual layout based on pilot feedback
definition_of_done: Checklist and log templates updated
Readability and space for notes improved
Final versions approved by project lead

backlog.task: Update SOP and training materials after pilot
definition_of_done: SOP updated with agreed changes
Training materials adjusted to reflect final process
Version control and change log recorded

backlog.task: Document compliance alignment and risk assessment
definition_of_done: Short memo mapping protocol steps to correctional procedures
Key legal and safety risks listed with mitigations
Reviewed by prison management or compliance representative

backlog.task: Prepare final project summary and rollout recommendation
definition_of_done: Summary of objectives, approach, and outcomes drafted
Recommendation on wider rollout and next steps included
Shared with all stakeholders for sign-off

threads_plan.thread_goal: Align on current process, main gaps, and project scope before design work starts.
threads_plan.trigger: Kickoff message announcing the project and asking for input on current practices.

mandatory_decisions.decision: Agree on the exact scope of the protocol (which units and types of detainees).
Confirm the current-state process map in A1 as the baseline for design.

threads_plan.thread_goal: Define practical health risk indicators and observation checklists for officers.
threads_plan.trigger: Biophysicist shares draft indicators and asks for operational feedback.

mandatory_decisions.decision: Approve the final list of health risk indicators for inclusion in A2.
Agree on the structure and length of the observation checklist A3.

threads_plan.thread_goal: Lock down the SOP, logging template, and filing workflow.
threads_plan.trigger: Management assistant posts draft SOP and log template for review.

mandatory_decisions.decision: Sign off on the escalation steps and responsibilities in SOP A5.
Confirm the final format and storage routine for the health log A4.

threads_plan.thread_goal: Plan and execute the pilot, then consolidate feedback and improvements.
threads_plan.trigger: Proposal to start the pilot in one unit with a defined start date.

mandatory_decisions.decision: Select the pilot unit, dates, and participating staff as per A6.
Agree on which changes from the pilot feedback A7 will be applied before rollout.

channel_rituals: Daily async check-in where each participant posts yesterday's progress, today's focus, and blockers.
Twice-weekly quick review of any incidents or edge cases to see how the draft protocol would have applied.
Weekly summary message consolidating decisions, updated artifacts, and next priorities.
Post-pilot retrospective thread to capture what worked, what did not, and concrete follow-up actions.
